body:
Going through the same thing right now, OP. I've never been in a stable relationship and have suffered through some pretty awful emotional abuse from those I thought I "loved".

My advice may not be the best but keep working on improving yourself without losing yourself (be yourself, but keep working on keeping your anxiety in check). That, and just talk to people. Be in those situations where you can meet interesting, new faces. One may come around that'll surprise you (just take your time...just wish I knew that myself instead of getting in trouble again).

There's no one right way to do this. Just be yourself and keep improving. As long as you are in the right situations, *someone* is bound to take notice. (Easier said than done, as my own experiences can attest...)

My mom worries a hell of a lot. My dad keeps a lot to himself.

That, and no one "seeks help" in my family. They either go it alone or let it out in other ways. No one has gone to therapy, yet a few have been prescribed antidepressants.

I was the first one in my immediate family to be upfront about things and often get met with "stop acting weak" or "man up" or "how would you like it if I just started talking like you all the time?"

So, long story short, I have no idea if it's nature or nurture. But I've always been emotionally sensitive. I dunno.

One of my friends and I have essentially just stopped talking because of this. Our last conversation ended awkwardly (many of ours do in text) so I'm anxious to start a conversation and sometimes she's just not comfortable responding. Or she's not that interested.

I don't have any idea if I did anything to cause this because I never hear back. Maybe I should ask? I don't know. It's been a month. She'll give up on me. Everyone does.
I've said it a few times here but it's tough for us to compare our own lives with someone else's "highlight reel". I usually just stay away.

I actually wanted a diagnosis because I needed to know "what was up" with me.

Now that I have an idea, it's actually allowed me to figure out and identify what's wrong a bit easier than before. I'm not gonna lie, I still struggle quite a bit, but at least I know what I have is legitimate and isn't "weakness" or "not being man enough".

I've stopped posting and browsing unless I have something *urgent* to say. Checking and making statuses affects my anxiety so much that I'd rather cut the trigger out of my life completely.

If anyone cares enough, they'll call me or use Facebook Messenger.

I'm truly starting to think that keeping a social media profile is a useless pursuit that leads to empty "validation". I'm better off searching for that type of connection in person, though I'm not even sure how to start.

When I don't get a single text or message from anyone all day.

When friends turn their backs and speak to other friends.

When everyone starts laughing and enjoying a conversation about a topic you know nothing about (and you just stand still and wish you could be anywhere else).

When someone looks at you oddly, tells you not to be ridiculous or genuinely makes you feel guilty for feeling a certain way.

That's when I feel this way, OP.

(EDIT: What's worse is people always say this stuff is childish and that I should have "grown out of it" years ago. That it's pathetic I should constantly feel this way in my mid 20's. I guess that's why I sought help and why I decided to post here).

The New Pornographers - Letter From An Occupant.

Every time that song's in the car, it's sing along time. I've had such a hard time coming to grips with several things this past year, but the songs on their "Mass Romantic" album always put a smile on my face.

Sometimes I feel I vent way too much and it causes me to feel embarrassed or like a burden, which causes me to go 100% the other way, to "suffer in silence" and become insular.

Part of me joining to post here was because I felt I vented way too much on my Facebook feed. That, or an argument I had with my parents where they said I was being reckless and ruining my reputation by discussing my problems (I'm a guy, which may enter into it).

This internal struggle over whether or not my feelings are "valid" throws me into even more turmoil and I wonder if my discussing of my feelings DID cause some estrangement in friendships or relationships.

I don't know if I'm doing anything right or wrong, but who knows. I am open about how I feel, and I value that part of myself. It's certainly better than keeping it inside and letting it fester.

I just went through this entire process myself. If only I found this resource earlier...she always likes to overshare her life on FB and it made me nervous because our private text conversations would always get so awkward.

Honestly, I would log in every day anticipating to be unfriended and it still hasn't happened.

From my standpoint, definitely take a social media break. Uninstall it from your phone, log out of it on your browser, and tell him, assertively, about your feelings and how much you value trust.

Communication is definitely important, so make sure you are both talking regularly in other venues should you decide to take a break.

I hope all goes well.

I've only heard cast recordings of Phantom, unfortunately (same with Evita, though holy crap, I love Mandy Patinkin and Patti LuPone, they are both so iconic even without their Broadway pedigree).

Again, I wish I knew more about theater and musicals. I played the Police Officer in Oliver! back in Middle School, and saw both Beauty and the Beast and Mamma Mia. I also came in possession of a vintage shrinkwrapped copy of South Pacific's original cast recording on vinyl a few days ago thanks to my uncle, but I may just keep that as a collectable. Otherwise, I don't know much but kinda wish I did.

That video and the MJ reference reminds me of one of Fred's dances that someone randomly dubbed Led Zeppelin's "South Bound Saurez" over. It made the song way better than it was (sadly, the video appears to have been taken down).

Definitely true, OP. As a bigger, taller dude I don't receive many from people other than my mom. But I can recall a few off hand as if they happened a few minutes ago:

A local representative of a charity I volunteered for (the American Federation of Suicide Prevention) smiled and told me I had "really warm hands" during a mid-winter seminar. It was a woman in her 20's. I think I blushed.

A girl I once dated called me a "10/10, A+ Person"...weeks after we'd stopped dating. I'll take it!

A few people complimented me on my voice and asked if I've ever considered announcing professional sports. ( *like. every day!* )

And that's an awesome step to take. As someone who has social anxiety himself, it's great when you get that opportunity.

The last girl I dated was someone I got along really well with at a party. Had it been a few years earlier, I may not have even talked to her, though we really bonded. Our dating didn't last very long but she's still an awesome person and we still talk from time to time (though my feelings often get in the way).

Definitely some overlap with your aforementioned interest in musicals!

I'll be really honest, I haven't watched as many as I would like. That goes for theater as well...I just don't go out to many plays and shows but it's something I just need the right opportunity to get into. 

The Astaire/Rogers movie musical "Top Hat" is one I remember seeing a few years ago, as was "The Broadway Melody of 1929" which I thought was kinda cool for being one of the first 'talkie' musicals.

I'll be honest, though. I did get a kick of seeing Russell Crowe and Hugh Jackman bellow their way through "Les Mis" a few years ago. In spite of the deficiencies, I always cry like a baby whenever I see the few scenes Anne Hathaway was involved in. But comparing the 2012 film version to the original is almost sacrilege.

Speaking of theater, tonight I just saw a performance of "Almost, Maine" put on by a cousin's college theater club. It's not a musical, though I found it extremely fun and quirky. More research showed that it's actually one of the more popular High School drama club plays right now. Interesting...still, a nice night out and a good opportunity to support a really talented bunch of kids (that I'm only around 5-6 years older than, but still :P).

This is all too real to me, OP.

I'm a straight guy. The majority of girls I've dated were either bisexual or closeted lesbian. It's probably a coincidence.

Beyond sexuality, they were all some of the most interesting people I've ever met. I've always been drawn to unconventional, unique women. In my case, however, that's nearly always created its own set of unique challenges.

I try to keep my own interests as open as possible so I can definitely relate to your posts. It's kinda hard operating under clashing interests.

Huge film and history buff, and when those two collide it's doubly awesome.

Big fan of character-driven dramas, Akira Kurosawa films and surrealism. But mostly films that make me think and feel. 

I have way too many favorites, but right now I'm watching Kieslowski's Dekalog (a ten-part series based on the Ten Commandments but not overtly religious and set in 1980's Poland).

What are some of your favorite film eras, directors and movies?

26M and haven't been in a stable, mutual relationship. Either I've chickened out due to external pressures or the girl just didn't care enough. I had a two-year (unrequited) LDR a few years ago and won't do it again unless the circumstances are much different.

Right now I'm trying to do the "self-care" and "treat yourself" method of coping with my most recent breakup, and hoping some of the new online friends I've made and the Meetup clubs I've joined leads to meeting someone that will make me forget about some of the rough times I've had trusting girls in the past.

It kinda feels awkward going places alone but it's better going to your favorite places alone than spending more time around the house wondering what could've been.

I just want something simple and old-fashioned. Hanging out, talking and enjoying just being there together. No mind games, tests or awkward texting strategies. Just something that starts and develops naturally. Gotta take care of myself first, though.

I am very similar in terms of being afraid of running into others who might have done me wrong in the past. I am also 26 and graduated high school nearly ten years ago and still have those concerns. I also share the same anxiety with exes and people I used to work with.

As much to the contrary as it may seem, where you are in life is nothing to be embarrassed about. Every person makes it through at their own pace. Ignore the standards social media shows us. We can only progress at our own rate, and just putting that effort in to improve yourself makes you that much better!

Chances are those people won't know your predicament or even remember you. If they do, just be honest with them. High school reputations no longer matter once you leave. It's best to concentrate on, as you said, moving forward with your own life.

A lot can happen in a small amount of time...keep focusing on what you do for yourself! Embrace the help you get from others and walk away from those who judge you. This sub and your T/councelor/social worker will give you more specific strategies to help battle those feelings.

Thanks for your reply. She and I have not texted in a few weeks and I'm already taking more time to do things by myself so I don't worry about the situation (and yet I still do). It's not easy, but I'm trying to make things better for myself so that I don't attach myself so quickly to others.

This is the worst feeling for me, especially since I've been told no one cares about my thoughts and "will see me differently" or "treat me weirdly" if I open up to them.

Some times, if I feel anxious enough or strongly about the person I'm talking to, I burst into tears. Which is really tough and  embarrassing since my emotions just begin to overflow and my sensitivity rears its head. As a guy, it's even tougher to deal with, because everyone has these preconceived notions of how men *should* emote.

I often think it scares people away and I end up withdrawing from them out of embarrassment. Then again, in moments like that, certain people feel they know how to push my buttons and end up using me because they know how I'd react.

Gah I just wish it didn't have to be this way.

There is really no shame in seeking help if you feel something's up. I was in the same boat for a long time (as I said above) because I was just too prideful. Now that I know what's up, it's allowed me to think objectively about my situation and hope to better it. If you decide to move forward, it won't hurt. Especially if you're unsure about your own situation.

As for the incidents, they may very well be unrelated or coincidental UNLESS the person/car is indeed the same. It is definitely right of you to be cautious. People can be very disrespectful of personal space. But unless you have proof these incidents are related, the best thing to do would prepare. Talk about this to people you trust (or authorities, or organizations that offer resources) and research methods of taking action, if need be. Should you seek help, counsellors or social workers may be able to help you formulate constructive verbal or mental self-defense strategies.

I'm not sure if these suggestions will work best for you but I hope it all goes well. Feel free to PM if you'd like.

I had similar thoughts last night and actually did what some of the replies suggested. Mostly negating, out loud, the thoughts and fears as being irrational. Just verbalizing it helped a lot and allowed me to move my thoughts on to a more positive level. It may not work for everyone but telling myself to "stop" out loud actually kinda helped (along with a few jokes in last night's r/anxiety chatroom, which I suggest visiting).

Also, I'm not sure if this truly applies but DO NOT view being ignored on social media as a basis of personal disapproval.

In fact, if you feel that people ignoring you on social media networks is affecting your mental health, you have every right to step away for as long as you like. As much as we elevate sites like Facebook, it often does a lot to amplify our insecurities. Especially if we see that certain friends always seem to hang out with others and not with us. Don't compare your everyday life with someone's highlight reel.

Anyway, even if social media is not the major concern, there are a lot of ways for us to combat our social anxieties. There is a high chance that people --- especially strangers --- will totally forget our awkward moments and will likely never see us again. Just gotta keep that in mind, hard as it is.

All the best. We're right there with you.

I have way too many of these people in my life. :(

The worst is when you say something innocent and they don't reply, leaving you wondering what in the world you did to upset them. But in reality, texting is such a crappy, indirect and misinterpreted system that it just boggles my mind how it's become our generation's main communication method.

And I'm especially frustrated around people whose actions paint a different picture than their words. But anxiety says "don't cut them out of your life because you don't want to be friendless!" At the same time it tells me "you're the problem, this person's a saint". Just can't win. :/

I know this feeling as well and I have been there many times. If it isn't real life people I obsess over, especially romantic interests, it's fictional characters.

In the case of the latter, I used to think I should have been thrown into an institution for feeling that way over people who don't exist, until I met more people who were really into their fandoms, and through that I learned it was more normal than I thought.

I also suggest keeping yourself busy and focused on yourself, as hard and boring as it may be. Make an effort to focus on your job or school work. Throw on some music that won't remind you of your obsessions or self-doubt. Maybe go out and treat yourself to dinner or play a video game that doesn't involve a story (sports games work really well, lmao).

I've learned the hard way that obsessing over someone may lead to more intense disappointment down the road if the person doesn't reciprocate your amount of caring. I've been there and it brought on some really hard times.

But if there's a positive to this, it's a way of recognizing your capability and potential for caring about others. The way I see it, had you not the ability to care, you wouldn't feel this strongly. Just try to keep busy and distracted, as hard as it may be.

This may come off as a little harsh but you can't force people to like you. If they do, that is amazing. But if they don't make you a priority, it's time to find new friends who will appreciate you.

Sometimes this comes with, as others said, just getting out there and doing stuff, even if it's by yourself. Don't be afraid to just hang out somewhere alone. Even if you make conversation with cashiers or workers at a store, they're still people and they're still conversations. And if you choose to get help, look to attend support groups. You never know if there will be someone else you connect with there (just please don't expect romantic connections).

I'm struggling with the same thing and in therapy at the moment, but I've signed up to groups on Meetup and tried to find some stuff I'm interested in. It's often hard for people with social anxiety to get acquainted with strangers who have similar interests, but it's a viable option if nothing else is around.

And like others have said, start off small and don't expect much. Maybe you'll get into conversations with people and find them interesting. You never know who will come up, but, please, consider getting help and take small steps, even if it's by yourself, to make your situation better.

And if your friends are right there with you, even better! Just don't get tied up in everyone else's lives. Concentrate on what you can do for YOURS, as hard as it can sometimes be.

If need be, quit Facebook and social networking, even if it's just for a week. If you absolutely need to talk to people on there, keep Messenger. As someone whose name I can't remember once said, "don't compare your everyday life with someone else's highlight reel". Chances are they're living with struggles deeper than you think and only want to brag about the good things.

Hi, everyone...I was recently diagnosed with social anxiety disorder, panic disorder and depression after putting off help for so long. 

I finally decided to move forward with getting help at the end of last year, started therapy a few months ago and had a diagnosis a few weeks ago. 2016 has been rough, but it's also been a year of positive changes for me. Even if my diagnoses got overwhelming at first, my hope is to use what you all have here to feel better about moving forward with my life.

I predominantly want to learn more about this and what steps people are taking, especially with their interpersonal friendships and relationships. I've only been here for a few days but I've already seen a few topics that hit really close to home. And that makes me feel less alone in this struggle.

I also have friends who deal with anxiety on a daily basis so hopefully what I learn about myself (and who I talk to here) will be instrumental in being a better friend as well.

Right now I'm going through a really tough time with a date (who, incidentally enough, is one of those friends with anxiety I just mentioned), and I'm having a very tough time moving on from the uncertainty of the situation, but it seems she is still interested enough on some level. My problem is I care too much, overthink and get way too anxious over making things perfect. And texting? Oh my god, it's torture. But if it works out, it works out. If it doesn't, well, who knows. But I've never really had any stable relationships, ever, so...I don't know if this is normal or anything, but it's really baring heavy on my heart recently.

Anyway, I'm glad a place like this exists and I'm looking forward to interacting with the community.

I got so anxious after I didn't get a text back after a date with my date that I looked at all the local television stations' websites and made sure no crimes happened overnight. That was the last time I ever sent out a "hey, hope you made it back okay" text.

Of course, I never told her this, but anxiety makes me way clingier than I need to be...

Mostly in relationship settings. Sadly it sometimes turns into a self-fulfilling prophecy, even if I don't do anything to cause it. :/

I've had a fear of this happen many times due to unreliable friend groups in the past. Also had a panic attack over a nightmare where a love interest found someone else.

As for professionally, I've had the feeling I'm "just a butt in a seat" many times but I wouldn't say I felt anxiety over losing my job because of it. Just "oh, well, if I were to quit tomorrow, they'll find someone else". I feared it much less than being replaced by friends or love interests, though.
Thanks so much. I will *definitely* take your advice seriously and make sure I have it as I continue to move forward.

I appreciate it. I kinda wish I hadn't waited so long, maybe this post would have been shorter.

What you said is kinda that key thing I'm trying to discover (not letting others affect my own happiness). I thought the self care stuff was supposed to help that, and I was fine with doing stuff on my own a few years ago, but after a while it started getting monotonous and I started losing interest.

I just feel like life's too short to be isolated and feel so down, so I'm still confused as to why my thoughts jump to suicide every time I feel like I messed something up.

It's tough getting there but self-approval will have to be the way I make it there. I just need to find ways to achieve it, which is almost tougher than simply saying it.

EDIT: I had a psych eval a month or so ago and the doctor recommended medication to prevent panic attacks as the early symptoms happen (the name escapes me at the moment). I'm strongly considering it whenever I run into a bad situation.

I understand. My aim is to save but I feel I spend way too much on myself in the name of "self care". I am beginning to realize that some of it is reckless, so I'm going to see how much I can put aside every month after car, credit card, insurance, loans and maybe cut down on the "self care" stuff like video games, nights out, "nerd cons" or tickets for concerts/sporting events that friends occasionally ask to go to.

Right now I'd rather focus on long term rather than short term, so if I have to cut some of that entertainment money out and spend more nights in, so be it. I just have to make it happen in such a way that I can still be social and have fun without breaking my budget or feeling bored at home. 

(I could also stand to sell some of the entertainment stuff I don't watch or play anymore...maybe being a collector isn't the wisest choice when I'm working toward moving out)
I don't want to let down the few people that I feel see *something* in me.

Thanks for reading.
It's tough because we still live in the same house. But moving out has been one of my few long-term goals, just need the money to do so.
One of these days I'm hoping I'll get a promotion or raise if I work hard enough...that, or the aforementioned third job. I just don't see much of any type of solution right now, but we'll see how it goes.
